name: Vectrex built-in vector display (Samsung 240RB40)

timing.ref: Malban, Vectrex tutorial II (30 000-cycle round, 1/50 s); Roger Boesch via crtgang (200-400 vectors per frame)

beam.model: charge per mm of line = beam current / speed; a stopped beam at each line end for dwell_s
beam.ref: Malban: drawing slower is brighter, length = strength x time; Vectrex32 manual: a bright dot at the end of lines

phosphor.type: P4 (white, assumed: the standard black-and-white TV phosphor)
phosphor.persistence: medium short: each frame shows only the lines drawn in it

faceplate.note: a black-and-white TV tube behind the Vectrex's screen bezel; glossy front (assumed)

brightness.note: the knob on the back of the display: the beam current at full intensity, relative to its maximum

facts: Samsung 240RB40: 9 in (240 mm diagonal), 90°, a black-and-white TV tube with no mask (Vectrex service manual)
each line at a strength (speed) for a time (scale); slower = brighter, a bright dot at each end (Malban; Vectrex32 manual)
about 200-400 vectors per frame before the refresh slows and the picture flickers (Roger Boesch)
